text: If dichloromethane (DCM) and water $(H_{2}O)$ are used for differential extraction, which one of the following statements is correct ?
options: DCM and $H_{2}O$ would stay as upper and lower layer respectively in the separating funnel (S.F.)
DCM and $H_{2}O$ will make turbid/colloidal mixture
DCM and $H_{2}O$ would stay as lower and upper layer respectively in the separating funnel(S.F).
DCM and $H_{2}O$ will be miscible clearly
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Density of DCM = 1.39 and density of $H_{2}O = 1.0$.
Dichloromethane (DCM) is a denser solvent than water. Therefore, when a mixture of DCM and water is allowed to settle in a separating funnel, the DCM forms the lower layer due to its higher density, while the water forms the upper layer. The two solvents are immiscible, meaning they do not mix and form two distinct layers.

So, the correct answer is :

Option C : DCM and $H_{2}O$ would stay as lower and upper layer respectively in the separating funnel(S.F).

text: Two pi and half sigma bonds are present in :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In molecular orbital terms, a pair of electrons in a bonding orbital counts as one bond and a single electron as half a bond; electrons in antibonding orbitals cancel bonding ones of the same type.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (13 electrons): $σ1s^{2}\qquad σ^{\ast }1s^{2}σ2s^{2}σ^{\ast }2s^{2}π2p_{x}^{2}=π2p_{y}^{2}σ2p_{z}^{1}$. The filled $π2p_{x}$ and $π2p_{y}$ give two $π$ bonds and the single electron in $σ2p_{z}$ gives half a $σ$ bond (bond order 2.5).

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (15 electrons): $σ1s^{2}\qquad σ^{\ast }1s^{2}σ2s^{2}σ^{\ast }2s^{2}σ2p_{z}^{2}π2p_{x}^{2}=π2p_{y}^{2}π^{\ast }2p_{x}^{1}$. This is one full $σ$ bond and two $π$ bonds less half a $π$ bond, i.e. one $σ$ and one and a half $π$ bonds; its bond order is also 2.5, but the half bond is of $π$ type.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ has one $σ$ and two $π$ bonds, and $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ has one $σ$ and one $π$ bond.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot

text: Which of the graphs shown below does not represent the relationship between incident light and the electron ejected from metal surface ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Einstein's photoelectric equation: $\text{KE}_{\max }=hν-hν_{0}=E-𝜙$, where $𝜙=hν_{0}$ is the work function and $ν_{0}$ the threshold frequency.

(A) KE versus energy of light: KE is zero up to $E=𝜙$ and then rises linearly, starting from the threshold on the energy axis. This graph is correct.

(B) KE versus frequency: $\text{KE}=hν-hν_{0}$ is a straight line of slope $h$ that starts at $ν_{0}$, not at the origin. A line through the origin would mean electrons are ejected at every frequency, so this graph is wrong.

(C) KE versus intensity: KE depends only on the frequency, so at a fixed frequency it stays constant as the intensity changes. This graph is correct.

(D) Number of electrons versus frequency: no electron is ejected below $ν_{0}$; above $ν_{0}$ the number is set by the intensity, not by the frequency, so it jumps to a constant value. This graph is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot

The major product of the following reaction is

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Alcoholic KOH performs $α$ - $β$ elimination with halides.

The carbon which is attached to Br atom is called $α$ carbon.

Here, two $α$ carbons are present. Let's call them $α_{1}$ and $α_{2}$. 

In case of $α_{1}$ carbon, H elimination can take place either from $β_{1}$ or $β_{2}$ carbon. But as we know always more stable product is formed from a reaction. Here if H is removed from $β_{1}$ carbon then a $π$ bond is created which will participate in resonance with benzene ring and product will be more stable. But if H is removed from $β_{2}$ carbon then the created  $π$ bond will not participate in resonance with benzene ring so product will be less stable.

In case of $α_{2}$ carbon, H elimination can take place either from $β_{2}$ or $β_{3}$ carbon. But as we know always more stable product is formed from a reaction. Here if H is removed from $β_{2}$ carbon then a $π$ bond is created which will participate in resonance with the $π$ bond associated with the $α_{1}$ carbon so product will be more stable. But if H is removed from $β_{3}$ carbon then the created $π$ bond will not participate in any resonance so product will be less stable.

text:
The correct structure of product 'P' in the following reactions is : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Asn–Ser, asparagine is the N-terminal residue (free $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$) with a side-chain amide $-\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$, and serine is the C-terminal residue (free $-\mathrm{COOH}$) with a side-chain $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$.


[IMG]

Excess acetic anhydride with $\mathrm{NEt}{}_{3}$ acetylates the nucleophilic groups: the free $α$-amino group becomes $-\mathrm{NHCOCH}{}_{3}$ and the serine $-\mathrm{OH}$ becomes the ester $-\mathrm{OCOCH}{}_{3}$.

The side-chain amide nitrogen is not acetylated because its lone pair is delocalised into the adjacent C=O group, and the $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group is left unchanged.

P therefore has the acetylated amino group and the intact $-\mathrm{CONH}{}_{2}$ side chain on the asparagine residue, and the $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OCOCH}{}_{3}$ group on the C-terminal serine residue, which is structure (B); structure (A) has the residue order reversed.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
The major product of the following reaction is : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$ removes chloride from $\mathrm{Ar}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}$ (Ar = 3-methoxyphenyl), generating the primary carbocation $\mathrm{Ar}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})-\mathrm{C}^{+}\mathrm{H}_{2}$.

A 1,2-hydride shift from the neighbouring CH converts it into the much more stable tertiary carbocation $\mathrm{Ar}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{C}^{+}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}$.

The cationic carbon is the third carbon of the side chain, so intramolecular Friedel–Crafts alkylation at a ring carbon ortho to the side chain closes a five-membered ring carrying the $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}$ group: a 1,1-dimethylindane. The methyltetralins of (B) and (D) would need ring closure by the unrearranged primary cation.

Of the two ortho positions, the one para to $-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$ is activated by its $+R$ effect and unhindered, whereas the one between the two substituents is crowded; ring closure therefore occurs para to $-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$ (closure at the crowded position would give (C)). Loss of $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ restores the aromatic ring, and water in step (ii) only decomposes the aluminium chloride complex.

The product is 5-methoxy-1,1-dimethylindane, with $-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$ para to the ring carbon bearing the $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}$ group.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The total number of isomers for a square planar complex
 [M(F)(Cl)(SCN$)(NO_{2})$] is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{F})(\mathrm{Cl})(\mathrm{SCN})(\mathrm{NO}{}_{2})]$ is a square planar complex of the type $[\mathrm{Mabcd}]$, which has 3 geometrical isomers: with F fixed, the ligand trans to it can be Cl, SCN or $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$.

Two of the ligands are ambidentate: thiocyanate binds through S ($\mathrm{M}-\mathrm{SCN}$) or N ($\mathrm{M}-\mathrm{NCS}$), and nitrite binds through N ($\mathrm{M}-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$) or O ($\mathrm{M}-\mathrm{ONO}$), giving $2\times 2=4$ linkage combinations.

Each linkage combination has 3 geometrical isomers, so the total number of isomers is $4\times 3=12$.

The plane of a square planar complex is a plane of symmetry, so none of these isomers is optically active and no optical isomers are added.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot
